HG17-fxw1:
Sober induction: 3–5 minutes

Practise reading this slowly into a recorder, or reading it aloud, or if you can learn it and use silent words. Choose to use one of the three anchors – sound, bodily contact or two hands - throughout and choose an opening phrase. Whenever the words below refer to ‘the anchor’ use the one you’ve chosen. Pause for a few moments at the end of each paragraph. Don’t read aloud the instructions for how to do the reading.

Let your eyes settle somewhere in the room, somewhere they can rest for a little while, and notice the difference between looking for something and letting what is already there come into view.

As you notice the surface beneath you, notice the feel of the contact, the pressure, whatever you can actually feel. And while you notice that, a sound may reach you, or a breath may draw your attention, without needing you to arrange either one.

There’s time to do this.

It might be that a thought about something that’s happened during the day is still with you, or perhaps there’s a thought about doing this properly. Whatever is there, can you find it in yourself to turn your attention back to the anchor, even if there is a thought there?

and when you do come back, you may find one detail that holds your interest, something about the sound, or the contact, or that particular way of listening, and let attention stay with it long enough to become curious

Perhaps you can give yourself the time that you might give to someone dear to you who has begun to speak and hasn’t yet found the words. You can remain nearby, listening, without finishing their sentence for them

Let the phrase you chose come to mind, say it as an invitation, and notice how it is received

You can close your eyes, soften them or keep them open as you proceed. Let that be a choice you make. Listening may deepen while a sound from the room remains available in the background

Count slowly from 5 to 1, giving each number its own moment

5, perhaps notice again what you have chosen to be your anchor for today, 4, let attention gather around what you find, 3, leave a little space after the words, 2, listen into that space, without preparing an answer, 1, stay here for a moment

Bring to mind, lightly, your chosen concern. Or simply, stay with the wish to contact. Let it be present without rehearsing its whole story.

What do you notice now?

Allow yourself some time to notice what is coming. It might be sensations, words, images, feelings, the urge to move in some way or nothing clear yet.

Allow yourself some time to notice this, with or without words.
HG31-fxw1:
Reframing — changing the meaning without lying

Dishonest reframing declares that the problem was secretly good all along, so I prefer to ask myself questions that widen the meaning without lying, like: “What else could be true here?” or “What is this part trying to do for me?” or “How would my Nurturer reframe this?” or “How would my Protector reframe this?” or “How would my Leader reframe this?” and so on.
HG06-fxw1: There are already a lot of forces out in the world training your mind: advertising, fear, craving, screens, tribe, resentment, authority, loneliness and repetition. Self-hypnosis lets you work on it from the inside. In this way you will learn to befriend the deeper part of your mind and listen to it, opening up a whole new area of choice for you as an adult.
HG26-fxw1:
When this needs more support than a guide can provide

Remember, this is self-hypnosis, a relationship with yourself. If the situation calls for support, this guide isn't the right thing.

If you need help now: Get help now if you feel in imminent danger, very confused, or unable to keep yourself safe. Get help now if you have concerning physical symptoms (chest pain, fainting, etc.) You should seek professional help promptly if you have new or worsening suicidal thoughts, severe insomnia, new or worsening symptoms of mania or psychosis, or if dissociative symptoms are affecting your functioning. These are not problems that this guide will resolve in 4-12 weeks.
HG24-fxw1:
You want the hidden truth immediately

Refrain. Say, “First show me the capacity, and you can show me the content later.”

You keep daydreaming

Sit up and open your eyes. Then ask, “What real action am I avoiding with this fantasy?”
HG15-pw1:
You can rebel, but you can’t choose

This happens because when you were a child, your attention went into avoiding pain, reading danger, meeting expectations and keeping the bond, so you didn’t have the opportunity to explore what you like, what you want to try out and who you are. This is not a claim about one specific brain system but a practical way to look at it.

Sometimes you need to distance yourself for a certain time from the people or group that you normally get your answers from. But not for too long, as then you defeat the purpose of this exercise! The distance helps quieter preferences surface, so you can tell your own signal from the social echo.
HG15-pw2:
When you are a child, you will feel that you need to belong to a family in order to survive. That is why many people do things for their family, their religion, their romantic partner, their political tribe, their spiritual group, their institution or their online community that they otherwise wouldn’t do! Part of adulting is finding out where you sell yourself in order to belong, and then choosing your own ground, and learning that you can disappoint someone without disappearing. Because a large part of your subconscious mind, is made out of other people. This is why you are reading a self hypnosis guide!

Where am I betraying myself in order to belong?
